name: St. Francis Xavier Cathedral and Library
history: The parish traces its roots to Jesuit missionaries on the Wabash River in the 1730s, making it the oldest Catholic parish in Indiana; its surviving records begin in 1749. The present brick church, begun in 1826, stands on or near the site of two earlier churches. It was the cathedral of the Diocese of Vincennes from 1834 to 1898.
arch: A plain Greek Revival church of 1826 with a single front steeple. It sits beside George Rogers Clark National Historical Park in the Vincennes Historic District.
features: The first four bishops of Vincennes, including Simon Bruté, are buried here.
The Old Cathedral Library, built beside the church in 1840 for Bishop Bruté's 5,000-plus books, was the first library in Indiana.

look.d: A single steeple rises over the entrance, a landmark beside the Wabash for two centuries.
Bishop John Stephen Bazin's consecration here in 1847 was the first episcopal consecration held in Indiana.

fun: Locals simply call it "the Old Cathedral", though it has not been a cathedral since 1898.
journal: Older than the state it stands in. Quiet brick, a whole frontier remembered.

quiz.q: Which state's oldest Catholic parish is this?
When was the present church begun?

a: The first four bishops of Vincennes
